wins.text: Full-year adjusted net income surpassed $16 billion, up 27% YoY; adjusted RoTCE improved to 8.8%, a 180 bps improvement; adjusted revenues up 7%, strongest growth in over a decade
Banking had record revenues with M&A up 84% in Q4 and 30 bps YoY increase in IB wallet share; Banking RoTCE of 11.3% for the full year with positive operating leverage for 8th consecutive quarter
Markets delivered record full-year revenues surpassing 2020 performance; Equities revenues of $5.7B a record with prime balances up over 50%; full-year RoTCE of 11.6%
Repurchased over $13 billion in common shares during the year including $4.5B in Q4; total capital return of over $17.5 billion, most since the pandemic; CET1 at 13.2%

USPB returns more than doubled for the year reaching mid-teens; Branded Cards NCL at 3.6% and retail services at 5.73%, both at or below the low end of guided ranges; USPB positive operating leverage for 13th consecutive quarter

risks.text: Russia held-for-sale accounting treatment created a notable item that reduced reported EPS to $1.19 and RoTCE to 5.1% vs. adjusted $1.81 and 7.7%; ongoing Russia exit and Poland consumer business sale still pending final approvals
Efficiency ratio guidance shifted from 'below 60%' to 'around 60%' for 2026, acknowledged by management as a slight softening of prior commitment to allow for continued franchise investment
Regulatory consent orders remain outstanding with timing of full resolution explicitly described as 'up to the regulators'; data remediation work still ongoing

Potential credit card interest rate cap legislation raised during Q&A; management flagged risk of severe reduction in consumer credit access and $4 trillion in untapped card capacity at risk if enacted
Markets Q4 revenues down 1% YoY against tough comp; Markets expenses up 14% in Q4 driven by legal, compensation and technology; full-year RoTCE of 11.6% still below firm targets

guidance_items.detail: NII ex-Markets guided to grow 5%-6% in 2026, up from prior expectation of a slowdown from 2025's ~5.5% growth; driven by mid-single-digit loan and deposit volume growth
Targeting efficiency ratio of ~60% for full year 2026, with positive operating leverage expected for the firm and all 5 businesses
Targeting 10%-11% RoTCE for full year 2026, up from 8.8% adjusted in 2025
Card NCL ranges reaffirmed at same levels as 2025 guidance (Branded Cards ~3.6%, Retail Services ~5.73%); total firm deposits expected mid-single-digit growth
Expects to do more than $13B in buybacks in 2026 as it works CET1 down from 13.2% toward ~12.6% target (100 bps management buffer)

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential credit card interest rate cap legislation and its impact on Citi's card business
Specific timeline for full consent order resolution and whether Citi or regulators are the bottleneck
Competitive gap versus best-in-class peers in investment banking and capital markets and how long to close it
